summary: Sporting News live blog of Game 3 of the 2023 World Series at Chase Field, where the Texas Rangers beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 3-1 to take a 2-1 series lead. Corey Seager's two-run homer and a Marcus Semien RBI single in the third inning decided it, while Jon Gray relieved the injured Max Scherzer with three scoreless innings. The note also gives pregame lineup news, viewing info and 2023 MLB playoff results.
one_line: Rangers beat the Diamondbacks 3-1 in World Series Game 3, their ninth straight road playoff win, to lead the series 2-1.
key_facts: The Rangers beat the Diamondbacks 3-1 in Game 3 of the 2023 World Series on Monday, Oct. 30 at Chase Field in Phoenix, taking a 2-1 series lead.
Texas won its ninth consecutive road game of these playoffs.
In the top of the third, Marcus Semien hit an RBI single to score Nathaniel Lowe, then Corey Seager hit a two-run home run 421 feet to right field, making it 3-0.
Max Scherzer was pulled after 36 pitches and three scoreless innings with a lower back injury, possibly related to a comebacker that hit his lower back in the second inning.
Jon Gray earned the win in surprise relief, throwing three scoreless innings with three strikeouts and one hit allowed.
Brandon Pfaadt finished with four strikeouts and three earned runs on four hits and two walks over 5.1 innings.
Arizona out-hit Texas but went hitless with runners in scoring position until the eighth, when Geraldo Perdomo's RBI single drove in Emmanuel Rivera for the only run.
Aroldis Chapman escaped the eighth with a 6-4-3 double play after Corey Seager's backhand play on a Ketel Marte grounder.
José Leclerc closed the ninth, striking out Christian Walker and Tommy Pham swinging to end the game.
Adolis Garcia threw out Christian Walker at home plate in the second inning, then left in the eighth with an oblique injury; Travis Janowski replaced him in right field.
Evan Carter batted fourth, making him the fifth-youngest player in World Series history to do so, joining Juan Soto, Ty Cobb, Miguel Cabrera and Claudell Washington.
The Chase Field roof was open for Game 3, and first pitch was at 8:03 p.m. ET.
Fox carried the series with Joe Davis on play-by-play and John Smoltz as analyst; Ken Rosenthal and Tom Verducci reported from the dugouts.
Before Game 3, the series was tied 1-1 after Texas won Game 1 6-5 and Arizona won Game 2 9-1.
